newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone government denies massacre report.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone government denies massacre report.

text.p: Sierra Leone's government on Tuesday emphatically denied attackers had killed 150 people in the north, saying such reports could undermine its peace deal with rebels and investor confidence.
"The reports threatened to...undermine the increasingly cordial relations between the RUF (rebel Revolutionary United Front) and the government," presidential advisor Sherka Mansaray told Reuters.
The reports, from a witness and local newspaper, blamed unknown gunmen for attacks on Thursday in Kubehuna and Magbenka in Tonkili district, about 90 miles (145 km) north of the capital.

The army has noted scattered attacks in the area, which is notorious for banditry, but Mansaray said neither the government nor international representatives had found evidence to confirm the Thursday attack.
He said such reports could discourage donors, who have been showing increasing interest since the November 30 signing of the peace deal in Ivory Coast.

"Several donor countries have informed the government since the signing of the accord of their willingness to contribute to the government's plea for $1 billion to rebuild and resettle the country," he said. "These reports threaten to keep donors away."
President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah on Monday vowed to crack down on frustrated soldiers whom he said staged acts of lawlessness to undermine the peace accord.
